us: Bessent launches the economic campaign at Treasury
effects: ~60 designations · Five lifelines on notice · Bank sanction promised by Friday
iran: Madanizadeh: Tehran 'fully prepared' · Araghchi dismisses bluster
tldr: The promised D-Day arrived as scaffolding rather than a strike: five sectoral determinations covering crypto, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, roughly sixty designations across five jurisdictions, dollar-expulsion warnings and a 'cure period' — with no countries named, no Chinese banks touched and little market reaction. Bessent promised a major financial-institution designation by week's end; Tehran said it was fully prepared to counter the measures.

events.title: Bessent at Treasury: 'sever every economic lifeline… until Tehran stands alone'
events.summary: The 'economic D-Day' press conference landed as what Bessent himself called 'a warning shot.' No country was named for secondary sanctions, no timeline given — only a 'cure period' for states to cut ties, and 'no one is above the reach of US sanctions.' On Chinese banks: facilitators of Iranian oil revenue 'will be targeted,' but none were. Markets showed little reaction.

events.title: Five sectoral determinations; ~60 designations across five jurisdictions
events.summary: Treasury declared Iran's digital-assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors — its five remaining 'lifelines' — open to sanctions on any operator worldwide, and designated nearly 60 entities, vessels and individuals in the UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland. Several general licenses for remittances and cultural or academic exchanges were suspended; OFAC urged shipping to refuse Iran's Hormuz transit demands.

events.title: Trump phones world leaders; bank designation promised this week
events.summary: Bessent said Trump is calling leaders with 'specific requests' to cease trading with Iran, that Treasury is 'level setting' through quiet diplomacy, and that 'you will see a major announcement of a financial institution being sanctioned by the end of this week.' Hegseth: Tehran will have 'no choice' but to return to talks on its nuclear program.

events.title: UAE ends all trade relations with Iran ahead of the announcement
events.summary: A close US partner that has absorbed Iranian attacks moved first: ending all trade ties days after its 19 August embargo measures. Bessent called the timing 'not coincident but likely causal' with Washington's campaign and predicted 'a broad array of countries' would follow.

events.title: Tehran: 'fully prepared' to counter the measures
events.summary: Finance Minister Ali Madanizadeh told IRINN Iran is fully prepared to counter sanctions aimed at countries keeping ties with it. Araghchi brushed the rollout off as bluster — nothing new against a country with, in state media's framing, 'a PhD in circumventing sanctions.' The rial held near its record low above two million to the dollar.

events.title: Pakistan's Munir brings mediation delegation to Tehran
events.summary: The army chief arrived at the head of an official delegation announced Sunday, touching on the sanctions threat among 'recent developments' — the first high-level mediation contact since the June memorandum's 60-day window lapsed.

dossier: Night count: 25th consecutive without confirmed strikes inside Iran; CENTCOM blockade accounting carried at 70 redirected / 3 disabled / 2 boarded. From Bessent's Q&A: asked why no immediate penalties — 'Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?'; 'we do not have infinite patience'; a Berlin Wall line aimed at Iranian soldiers whose paychecks are stopping; acting undersecretary Gene Wang flanked to signal secondary sanctions are not used lightly. An upcoming Xi–Trump meeting complicates direct action against Chinese banks. AP noted the largest trade partners left unpenalized were China, Turkey and the UAE. Pakistan's mediation follows its brokering of the June MOU.
